title: Oncall & Incident Response Guidelines
author: Anaïs Dupont
content:
Purpose:

This document supplements the primary on-call playbook with operational guidelines, runbook authoring standards, on-call rotation best practices, and communication templates for status pages and customer-facing messages. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and incident commanders.

Applicability:

- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, Private deployments, and supporting platform services (auth, billing, control plane).
- Use for production incidents; use test-runbooks and game-day guides for non-production exercises.

Severity classification (short reference):

- P0 (Critical): Total service outage or confirmed data/security breach. Immediate IC and war room.
- P1 (High): Significant customer-impacting degradation or imminent SLA breach. Rapid escalation.
- P2 (Medium): Limited impact (single region/customer). Triage and scheduled remediation.
- P3 (Low): Non-urgent issues or maintenance. Track in backlog.

Runbook authoring standards:

1) Single-responsibility: Each runbook should cover one failure mode. If multiple mitigations exist, split into separate steps with decision gates.
2) Preconditions: List required permissions, feature-flag keys, and safety checks (e.g., do not rollback during data-migration window).
3) Repro steps & detection: Include the alert name, example metric thresholds, and a short reproduction check.
4) Clear step ordering: Numbered steps, commands, and expected outputs. Prefer idempotent ops.
5) Verification: Minimal smoke tests (curl examples, health-check endpoints) to confirm recovery.
6) Escalation & contacts: PagerDuty escalation labels, secondary contacts, and on-call rotation owner.
7) Ownership: Document author and owner team with contact email.

Runbook lifecycle:

- Review cadence: Runbooks reviewed quarterly by service owner and SRE.
- Game-day validation: Each critical runbook must be exercised annually during game days.
- Deprecation: Mark runbooks deprecated when services are retired or runbook steps change irreversibly.

Typical runbook template (use as Confluence page template):

- Title
- Service / Owner
- Triggering alert(s) / Metrics
- Preconditions / Safety checks
- Immediate triage steps (quick checks)
- Mitigation steps (ordered with commands)
- Verification steps
- Escalation path and contacts
- Post-incident notes and links to related runbooks

Example runbook excerpt: Hosted API - Model hot-reload failure
Service owner: eng-serving-runtime
Triggers: hosted-api-model-hotreload-fail >=3 failures in 10m
Quick checks:
1) Check deploy logs: curl https://deploy-service.internal/api/recent?svc=hosted-api
2) Confirm model artifact availability in object store: aws s3 ls s3://models-prod/<model>/revisions/
Mitigation (if model load consistently fails):
1) Disable automatic hot-reload for the model (feature-flag: ff/model-hot-reload)
   ./ff-toggle --service hosted-api --flag ff/model-hot-reload --off
2) Restart worker pool handling the model: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/hosted-api-worker-<model>
Verification:
- Send sample inference request to the model and confirm success: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}'
Escalation:
- If not recovered in 20 minutes, page secondary and IC.

On-call rotations & handoffs:

- Primary on-call cadence: weekly (Mon 09:00 UTC start).
- Secondary: 4-week assignments; ensure overlap with primary handoff.
- Handoff checklist: recent incidents, ongoing mitigation items, runbook updates, scheduled maintenance in next 72 hours. Publish a 1-paragraph handoff note to oncall-calendar and incident channel.
- Burnout controls: enforce max 2 primary weeks per quarter per engineer where possible; team leads to redistribute pages when targets exceeded.

Paging & alerting guidance:

- Alert baselining: tie alerts to business-impacting metrics (error-rate, request success, queue depth). Use aggregation windows to reduce noise (5m for non-critical).
- Required alert metadata: severity, runbook link, primary owner team, and playbook link.
- Alert review: bi-weekly triage to retire flappers and adjust thresholds.

Communication templates (short):

Status page - initial acknowledgement:
Title: Investigating: Redwood Hosted API degraded performance
Time: <ISO timestamp>
Status: Investigating
Impact: A subset of inference requests are returning 5xx errors. We are investigating and will post updates.

Customer-facing support reply:
Subject: Incident update - Redwood Hosted API - Elevated error rates
Hi <CustomerName>,
We are currently investigating elevated error rates affecting inference requests. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will update you within 30 minutes. If you need immediate routing advice, please reply and we will prioritize.
Best,
Redwood Support

Status page - resolution:
Title: Resolved: Hosted API elevated error rates
Time: <ISO timestamp>
Status: Resolved
Impact: Error rates returned to baseline after mitigations. No customer data was impacted. Postmortem will be published within 72 hours.

Postmortem requirements & timelines:

- P0/P1: Postmortem draft within 72 hours; final postmortem with action items within 2 weeks.
- P2: Post-incident review within 2 weeks if customer impact occurred.
- Required sections: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root Cause, Mitigations, Remediations (actions with owners/ETA), Verification plan.
- Ownership: IC or service owner creates the postmortem; SRE reviews and publishes.

Game day program (ops exercises):

- Frequency: Quarterly with at least one cross-team full-scale exercise per year.
- Scenarios: Region outage, storage-tier failure, model-serving regression, control-plane auth outage.
- Metrics captured: detection time, MTTA, MTTR, communication latency, runbook accuracy score.
- Outcome: Action items created and tracked; runbooks updated where necessary.

KPIs & monitoring for on-call health:

- MTTA (by severity) - target: P0 < 5m, P1 < 15m.
- MTTR (by severity) - target: P0 < 1h, P1 < 6h.
- Pages per person per week - target < 2.
- Postmortem completion within SLA - target 100% for P0/P1.

Governance & review:

- Bi-annual review of playbooks, rotations, and alerting rules by SRE and Platform teams.
- After-action review after each P0 incident with executive summary to leadership.
- Exceptions: Any deviation from runbook or escalation order must be documented on the incident page and justified in the postmortem.

Document history:

- v0.9 (2025-06-10) - Drafted by Anaïs Dupont
- v1.0 (2025-09-01) - Published after SRE review
- v1.2 (2026-02-20) - Updated runbook standards and game-day cadence

End of document
